sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Health Monitoring Smartwatches and Smart Rings

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France–China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 30 May 1984, entered into force 21 May 1985; amended by the Additional Protocol of 26 November 2007) - active

France–China Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (signed 14 January 1984, entered into force 17 May 1985; amended by the Additional Protocol of 26 November 2007, applicable from 1 January 2010) - active

European Union–China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment (signed 30 December 2020; not yet in force, ratification suspended; monitored for future investment liberalization and protection benefits) - pending

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L. 227-1 to L. 227-20 (formation of the Société par Actions Simplifiée) and Articles L. 123-1 et seq. (registration with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) operated by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce in the territorial jurisdiction of the registered office; filings are submitted electronically through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form M0 (Demande d'immatriculation d'une personne morale au Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés), filed with the RCS via the Guichet Unique.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital applies to an SAS. The capital is fixed in the articles of association; cash subscriptions must be deposited into a blocked bank account in France or with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations until the company is registered. In-kind contributions must be valued by a commissaire aux apports unless all shareholders waive appointing an auditor. Funds are released only after successful registration and issuance of the Kbis extract.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: The shareholders, acting under Article L. 227-1 et seq. of the French Commercial Code, hereby (i) subscribe and accept the entire share capital comprised of ordinary shares as allocated in the articles of association; (ii) approve and fix the registered office at the address specified in the statutory documents, which shall serve as the legal seat for administrative and tax purposes; (iii) appoint the President and General Manager indicated in the annex to manage the company and sign all binding contracts; (iv) authorize officers to complete filings with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés, the tax authorities, and to obtain all licenses required for the smartwatch manufacturing site.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and execute the articles of association (statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaire public in the registered-office department, or a French corporate lawyer authorized to draft private statutes for an SAS.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the French-language AS statutes including legal name, corporate purpose (manufacture of health-monitoring smartwatches and smart rings), registered office, share capital, share classes, governance rules, president's powers, and share-transfer restrictions. All initial shareholders sign each statut page; any contribution of real property must be externalized in notarized deed.
required_dossiers: Company name reservation certificate issued by INPI (optional but recommended)
Passport or national identity card of each shareholder
Memory of corporate object and activity description
Lease agreement or domiciliation contract for the registered office
Signed draft statutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or reviewing counsel raises a legal deficiency, revise the relevant clauses, re-execute signatures, and resubmit the corrected dossier for the same review cycle without new fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open a blocked share-capital account and collect cash contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French licensed bank in the company's vicinity, or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations for statutory capital holding.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the name of the 'société en formation' and transfer all cash contributions from shareholders. Request the bank's attestation de dépôt des fonds, expressly stating the company name, capital amount, and the blocked nature of the account. If in-kind assets are contributed, arrange a commissaire aux apports valuation report before the RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening application
Draft statutes mentioning capital amounts
Identity documents of the authorized depositor
Shareholder contribution statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays issuance of the capital deposit certificate, escalate to the branch compliance officer or select another licensed bank; the certificate can be reissued after reconciliation of the deposit records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish the legal notice of incorporation in an approved legal gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) approved for the department where the registered office is located.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a legal notice to the JAL containing the corporate form, corporate name, registered office, share capital, corporate object, duration, and identity of the president. Arrange publication and retain the attestation de parution issued by the gazette.
required_dossiers: Draft legal notice text
Extract of the articles identifying the officers
Identification data of the company's future registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the gazette requests corrections due to inconsistencies, amend the factual details and republish the corrected notice; the publication date restarts from the corrected issue.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Assemble and submit the incorporation dossier at the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the official portal and complete the M0 registration form for an SAS. Upload all mandatory documents, declare beneficial owners (bénéficiaires effectifs), pay the applicable state and procedural fees, and submit the dossier electronically. The Guichet Unique transmits the file to the competent Greffe and to tax and social bodies.
required_dossiers: Form M0 duly completed
Certified copy of executed statutes
Capital deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt des fonds)
Attestation de parution in a legal gazette
Proof of registered-office address
Identity documents of the president and shareholders
Declaration of beneficial owners
Power of attorney if represented by a third party
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the platform rejects the submission for incomplete dossiers, identify the listed missing item in the online feedback, upload the corrected document, and resubmit within 24 hours; no records are lost.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain RCS registration and the Kbis extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered office acting as the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Greffe reviews the transmitted dossier, verifies legal conformity, registers the company, and issues the extrait Kbis, which constitutes official proof of legal existence and activity commencement clearance.
required_dossiers: Complete dossier transmitted by Guichet Unique
Registration fee payment confirmation
Compliance response to any Greffe observations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe issues an opposition or observation, file a supplementary explanation within the statutory period, correct the minor irregularities indicated, and request the registrar to proceed. If the Greffe refuses registration, apply to the President of the Commercial Court for a writ of mandamus under the applicable commercial procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with tax, social security, and make VAT active
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) and URSSAF via Guichet Unique transmission.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the Guichet Unique automatically transmits the Kbis data to DGFiP for corporate tax and VAT. Verify the French company creation's SIREN, SIRET, and the status of the French VAT number by checking in the tax support area on impots.gouv.fr and the INPI companies database.
required_dossiers: Extra Kbis
Registration number issued by RCS
Identity of the tax correspondent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If no SIREN, SIRET, or VAT allocation is received within fifteen calendar days after Kbis issuance, contact the Greffe and DGFiP service des entreprises to confirm the automatic registration; if necessary, file a supplementary declaration on the Guichet Unique to unblock the process.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Régionale de l'Économie, de l'Emploi, du Travail et des Solidarités (DREETS) and the local Mairie for premises occupancy; the RCS remains the main business register.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Déclaration d'ouverture et autorisation d'exploitation d'un établissement industriel dédié à l'assemblage d'appareils électroniques de santé (obtained under the local town planning code and the labour code).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full EIA report for low-impact wearable electronics assembly, provided no chemical surface treatment, battery manufacturing, or high-rate VOC-emitting coating is carried out. The project must be declared to DREAL under the ICPE regime only if solvent usage exceeds the annual regulatory trigger; otherwise a simple environmental registration or exemption letter suffices.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharged into municipal sewers must comply with French urban discharge limits (pH 5.5–9.5, COD and TSS thresholds) and have no metals or cyanide; volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions are limited to 20 mg C/m³ unless lower thresholds apply; WEEE/battery waste must be tracked and recycled in compliance with the French Environmental Code (Code de l'environnement) and EU REACH/RoHS–conforming material declarations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety approval by the Commission de Sécurité or a certified inspection bureau, confirming fire-extinguisher systems, emergency exits, and smoke compartments; structural load certification by a control office; workplace compliance with electrical installation standards NF C 15-100; and mandatory health clearance references from CARSAT and the competent occupational health service establishing the medical monitoring system for employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via the impots.gouv.fr portal and the Online TIN (Numéro de TVA Intracommunautaire) validation system; corporate income tax filings are made through the DGFiP professional online portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing a French SAS must file statutory incorporation documents with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) through the Guichet Unique (formalités.entreprises.gouv.fr). Upon completion, the entity receives its SIREN and SIRET numbers and the Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) issues a French intra-community VAT number enabling VAT registration and subsequent EU-wide transactions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No general check-the-box regime is available in France. The SAS is per se subject to French corporate income tax, but an irrevocable option may be filed to be taxed as a société de personnes (partnership) for five years; conversely, certain partnership forms may elect corporate income taxation. Hybrid mismatch rules under the French transposition of ATAD apply to deny deductions or impose recharacterisation where asymmetric tax treatment arises across jurisdictions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 85,000 annual taxable turnover for most supply-of-goods activities (EUR 37,500 for certain services), with the same threshold generally applying to foreign suppliers conducting distance sales of goods into France; reduced thresholds may apply for supplies of e-services under the OSS scheme.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing for domestic business-to-business transactions is phased in from 1 September 2026 for all entities (full deployment by 1 September 2027), requiring issuance through registered PDP platforms connected to the DGFiP's Chorus Pro clearance infrastructure. The existing real-time reporting for B2C transactions via the Fractional VAT Payment scheme utilises Chorus Pro and requires data transmission upon invoicing, with fiscal data clearing via APIs and digital stamping to authenticate and report transactions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A taxable person may apply a 0% VAT rate on the export of goods outside the EU when the goods are physically dispatched or transported to a non-EU destination, with the supplier retaining proof of export; services rendered directly to overseas customers and certain intangible supplies linked to exported goods may be zero-rated, provided the effective benefit or use is outside the EU and the general conditions of Article 260 undecies and CGI Article 262 are met.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or other transport document
Inward Remittance Certificate (or bank proof of settlement of export proceeds)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: False or abusive export zero-rating claims trigger full VAT clawback with interest at the statutory rate, a fine of up to 80% of the tax evaded in bad-faith cases, and potential criminal penalties of up to EUR 750,000 per manager and five years' imprisonment for tax fraud under Article 1741 of the French General Tax Code; administrative penalties include a 40% negligence penalty or 80% intentional misconduct penalty, and officers may be held jointly liable under Article L.267 of the French Tax Procedure Book.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (French central bank; Eurosystem/ESCB member) as monetary, financial-stability and balance-of-payments regulator, jointly with the Direction Generale du Tresor (French Treasury, Ministry of Economy and Finance), which administers foreign-exchange control ('relations financieres avec l'etranger') and direct-investment screening under Code Monetaire et Financier (CMF) Articles L151-1 to L151-4. Banque de France operates the TARGET2 settlement interface and collects statutory balance-of-payments statistics from resident companies; no separate exchange-control commission exists in France for ordinary corporate flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible in France: current-account and capital-account transactions are in principle unrestricted, with no FX licence, allocation, prior approval or repatriation ceiling for trade, profit, dividend or royalty remittances. France is bound by the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements and by EU Treaty freedoms. Residual frictions are limited to (i) the prior-authorisation regime for non-EU direct investments in sensitive or FDI-listed sectors (art. L151-3-2 CMF covering defence, cybersecurity, critical infrastructure and certain sensitive technologies; consumer-wearable electronics manufacturing is not listed); (ii) statistical reporting to Banque de France for selected cross-border financial flows; and (iii) the EUR 10,000 cash/bearer-instrument declaration at border crossings. Profit remittance is subject only to standard corporate formalities (audited accounts, board resolution, recipient tax-residence certificate) and separately to the applicable withholding-tax treaty regime; it is not an exchange-control hurdle.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender, mandatory repatriation or forced conversion ratio applies to French exporters. A French SAS may keep export receipts in EUR or in foreign-currency accounts ('comptes en devises') at any EU/EEA bank without central-bank approval. Remaining obligations are transparency-type: (i) monthly/periodic customs statistical declarations ('Declaration d'Echanges de Biens' / DEB) for extra-EU and intra-EU trade via the French Customs administration; (ii) a prior customs declaration for physical cash or bearer instruments equal to or exceeding EUR 10,000 transported across the border; and (iii) full traceability of export proceeds to underlying invoices and customers for AML/KYT purposes. No forced conversion timeline is imposed at any stage.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account ('compte de depot des fonds' for incorporation) and Operational EUR/USD Corporate Account with trade-finance and liquidity desk
Operational Corporate Account and documentary L/C desk; FX hedging and treasury services (ISDA-capable)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Credit Agricole (regional bank, e.g., Credit Agricole d'Ile-de-France, with Credit Agricole CIB for network and LC products)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account via the regional caisse, plus letters of credit and guarantees via Credit Agricole CIB in Paris
Operational Account and Greater-China corridor payments (SWIFT/LC) suited to HK/CN parent flows

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: CIC (Credit Industriel et Commercial, Groupe Credit Mutuel)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and SEPA treasury services

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale, Form 2065 series) and tax basis computations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via the 'Fiab' secure tele-transmission portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year fiscal year, the filing deadline is the second working day following May 1; for a non-calendar fiscal year, the deadline is no later than the third month following closing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 10% of net tax due plus monthly late payment interest of 0.20%; increase to 40% for bad faith; formal demand and enforced collection under Article 1728 and Article 1731 of the General Tax Code; continued non-compliance may trigger criminal charges and no automatic strike-off but significant administrative enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual financial statements by shareholders/sole shareholder and filing of accounts with the commercial registry (dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; official publication is handled through the RCS (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés) electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts must be approved by the shareholders within six months after fiscal year-end and filed with the registrar within one month of such approval; for a calendar-year entity satisfying June 30 approval, the filing must be completed no later than the four-month statutory window from the fiscal close
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing subjects the entity to an administrative delay penalty of €500 to €5,000 plus judicial enforcement; failure to file for two consecutive years allows the Public Prosecutor to request immediate court-ordered dissolution and administrative strike-off from the Trade and Companies Register; individual directors may also face criminal fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation and, where applicable, update of the beneficial owner declaration (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) sent to the commercial registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS beneficial owner file)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No separate French annual UBO re-declaration is required if no change occurs; the declaration is permanently maintained and every transfer or alternation resulting in beneficial ownership change must be filed within 30 days of each change; in practice the registered agent performs an annual verification before accounts filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or filing materially inaccurate beneficial owner data carries criminal fines up to €7,500 per individual and €37,500 per legal entity (C. mon. fin. L561-2-8); persistent non-compliance exposes the company to a judicial strike-off procedure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting decision approving financial statements and discharging management; associated statutory auditors' report if the audit threshold is exceeded is attached to the filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records / integrated into the annual accounts filing package presented to the Greffe; not filed as a standalone announcement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be held no later than six months after the close of the fiscal year; for a December 31 year-end, the ordinary decision must be adopted before June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to approve within six months does not trigger automatic strike-off alone, but renders the accounts filing impossible and exposes management to penalty for late/delayed accounts filing as referenced above.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Articles L227-9 and D227-1 of the French Commercial Code, an SAS must appoint a certified statutory auditor (Commissaire aux Comptes) when, at the close of the fiscal year, it exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds: total balance sheet assets above €4,000,000; net turnover above €8,000,000; average permanent headcount above 50 employees; a statutory auditor is also mandatory for any entity controlling or controlled by an entity itself subject to mandatory audit, regardless of the size thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual statutory accounts must be prepared under French GAAP (ANC Regulation 2014-03, Plan Comptable Général); IFRS as endorsed by the EU applies only to consolidated financial statements and is not mandatory for a standalone SAS; the accounting file must also be kept in the standard FEC (Fichier des Écritures Comptables) format.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: French law imposes no autonomous annual UBO re-filing but requires a permanent registry of beneficial owners held at the court registry; the registered agent and directors must review the 'Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs' on each movement of shareholding or management, and any change affecting the identity, nature of control, or percentage of economic rights of a beneficial owner must be filed with the Greffe within 30 days; for SAS companies holding more than 25% of the capital or control rights, every transfer of shares must be reflected in the securities movement register and formalized in the annual verification protocol before the annual accounts are filed.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Registre des décisions de l'associé unique ou des assemblées
Registre des résolutions annuelles et rapports de gestion
Minute Book of management and shareholder meetings

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% flat rate for fiscal years commencing on or after 1 January 2022 (ordinary corporate income tax, French: impôt sur les sociétés, IS). Reduced rate of 15% applies under conditions to taxable profits up to EUR 42,000 for enterprises with annual turnover below EUR 10 million.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Research tax credit (CIR) equal to 30% of eligible R&D expenditure up to EUR 100 million and 5% above; innovation tax credit (CII) equal to 20% of eligible innovation expenditure for small and medium enterprises up to EUR 400,000 per year. No statutory tax holiday applies to the IS regime; the main preferential mechanisms are the CIR/CII, certain provisional depreciation allowances for green and digital equipment, and the parent-subsidiary participation exemption for qualifying dividends.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 2065-SD (French: liasse fiscale) filed with the tax administration via the National Electronic Declaration Portal (French: téléprocédure) using the EDI or EFI mode; B2B filings use the EDI (Échange de Données Informatisées) protocol for regular non-resident taxpayers. Local taxes including business value added contribution (CVAE) and territorial economic contribution (CFE) are filed separately through the same electronic portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual income tax return must be filed no later than the second business day after 1 May of the year following the close of the fiscal year. For fiscal years ending on 31 December, the deadline is typically 2 May or the first business day thereafter if 1 May falls on a non-business day. Non-calendar fiscal years must file by the second business day after 1 May following the end of the fiscal year; a specific deadline is determined by the tax administration. Tax payments are made through four quarterly instalments, with the balance due by the statutory filing deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate name, legal form (SAS), registered address, French tax identification number (numéro de TVA intracommunautaire), SIREN/SIRET number, and contact details of the statutory representative.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the full legal name of the French SAS registered with the French Trade and Companies Register, the head office address in France, the French SIREN number, and the EU VAT number; include the non-resident parent company name and address in the annex only if required for transfer pricing declarations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2065 Box B: Fiscal Year and Activity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the fiscal year, the nature of the business activity, and the ISIC/NACE code (NACE 26.52 for manufacture of smartwatches and fitness wearables).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate the exact start and end dates of the French fiscal year of the SAS; state the principal activity as 'manufacture of watches and clocks' or 'manufacture of wearable electronic devices' in accordance with NACE Rev. 2 code 26.52 to align with the declared ISIC 2652 business scope.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2065 Box C: Profit or Loss Determination (Résultat imposable)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net corporate income tax result: accounting profit before tax, plus tax adjustments, moins deductible expenses, yielding the taxable income (résultat fiscal) subject to IS.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare only the French entity's own taxable income, computed under French GAAP; no consolidation with foreign group entities is permitted for normal taxation. Certain expenses invoiced by non-resident related parties must be added back if the arm's length nature and actual service provision are not demonstrated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2065: Reduced Rate Section (Régime du taux réduit)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Eligible taxable profits up to EUR 42,000 taxed at 15% where the entity satisfies the small and medium enterprise criteria (turnover below EUR 10 million, equity and ownership tests).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident controlled SAS, check eligibility: shareholders must be natural persons or SMEs meeting the EU definition, not a corporate group exceeding the ownership threshold; if a foreign parent controls the SAS, the reduced rate ordinarily does not apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2065-FC / Box 2065-N: Group Forms and Tax Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule FC for consolidated group statements, Schedule N for tax credit computation including the research tax credit (CIR) and innovation tax credit (CII).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the CIR/CII, include a technical description of eligible smartwatch R&D activities, payroll costs of French researchers, external research contracts with public or approved private research bodies, and clear traceability through the French entity's accounting records; the tax credit is applied against IS due and eligible for cash refund.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedules for fixed asset depreciation, amortisation, and provisions, including rates and periods adopted for production equipment used in smartwatch manufacturing activities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure depreciation is booked in the French statutory accounts of the SAS; no depreciation may be claimed for assets owned by related foreign entities even if economically used in France.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual transfer pricing documentation annexe (Formulaire 2059-A) required for companies exceeding EUR 400 million in turnover and for entities controlled by a foreign group; includes a summary of related-party transactions, methods applied, and functional analysis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident parent must ensure that the French SAS discloses all transactions with related enterprises established outside France, including intercompany purchase of components, toll manufacturing contracts, IP licenses, management fees, and financial transactions; provide the group allocation of profits and the arm's length policy.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of foreign source income and the imputation of foreign taxes under Double Tax Agreements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a French SAS receiving dividends from foreign subsidiaries, carry the gross foreign dividend, deduct the 95% participation exemption, and claim foreign withholding tax credit only where the applicable DTA provides for an imputation credit; attach the relevant DTA schedule and Form 2065-N.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the corporate income tax return triggers a penalty equal to 10% of the tax due if the return is filed within 30 days of the deadline, increased to 40% if filed after 30 days. Interest for late payment (intérêt de retard) accrues at the statutory monthly rate of 0.20% (annualised 2.69% for 2024) on the unpaid tax. Non-filing, incomplete filing, or fraudulent return carries a 80% tax penalty if the administration establishes deliberate evasion, plus a minimum EUR 1,000 bank charges penalty. For manifestly incorrect or omitted declarations, a 40% penalty applies. Circulaire BOI-CF-IOR-10-20 constrains the administration to impose additional sanctions for first-time non-compliance only in aggravated cases.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% on gross French-source dividends distributed by the French SAS to non-resident shareholders unless an EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption or a Double Tax Agreement reduction applies. For treaty-eligible shareholders, the rate is reduced, commonly to 0%, 5%, or 15% depending on the residence state and ownership threshold.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke relief, the non-resident shareholder must request a reduced rate or exemption before making the distribution by submitting a refund application on Form 5000 (Cérfa no. 10961) to the French tax office (DGFiP Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères) together with: (1) a certificate of tax residence (Certificate of Residence / Formulaire 5000) issued by the foreign tax authority, (2) proof of entitlement to the treaty benefits including shareholding structure and length of holding period, (3) the corporate resolution approving the dividend distribution, and (4) evidence that the beneficial owner does not fall under the anti-abuse provisions (e.g. principal purpose test or limitation on benefits clause). The French paying entity must apply the statutory 25% withholding to the gross dividend; the shareholder then files a reclaim or applies the reduced rate under the procedural regime set by Article 119 quater of the French General Tax Code for EU resident companies (exemption on a 5% cost base) and by the DTA network for third-country shareholders. From tax year 2023, the French tax authority requires the Form 5000 to be certified with an apostille for non-EU jurisdictions. Relief for arbitration and mutual agreement procedures is available under Article 60 of the French Tax Procedure Code (LPF).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on royalties: 33.33% for payments to non-residents for patents, trademarks, software copyrights, and know-how (Article 182 B of the CGI), reduced to a maximum of 0%, 5%, or 10% under DTA provisions (commonly 0% for EU under Article 119 quater for software and certain copyrights; 5% for royalties generally under the OECD Model Treaty). Statutory withholding on interest: 33.33% (Article 182 B ter) reduced to 0%, 10%, or 15% under DTAs and under the EU Interest-Royalties Directive (Directive 2003/49/EC) which applies to EU parent-subsidiary or sister companies, provided the recipient is the beneficial owner of the interest. Treaty relief is only available if the recipient qualifies as the beneficial owner and meets the administrative certification procedure (Form 5000). French domestic law imposes a deduction limitation for interest paid to related foreign companies under the thin capitalisation rules of Article 212 of the CGI: interest is non-deductible beyond the OECD debt-to-equity ratio (1.5:1), excessive EBITDA-based thresholds, and for interest paid to non-taxed related entities, subject to the 25% earnings stripping rule.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: The French transfer pricing documentation (fichier documentation) must be prepared and filed by companies exceeding EUR 50 million in annual revenue (CA HT, consolidated turnover) where the entity is controlled by or controls foreign enterprises, or where the entity is a French resident enterprise with related-party transactions exceeding EUR 400,000 in total per year; in all cases the full Master File and Local File must be established in French or English and be submitted upon request. The simplified transfer pricing annexe (Formulaire 2059-A) is mandatory for enterprises with annual revenue (excluding tax) of at least EUR 400 million. For a smartwatch manufacturing SAS, documentation thresholds are assessed separately; even below the EUR 400 million threshold, the company must maintain contemporaneous documentation for controlled transactions involving the import of components, assembly labour, IP financing, and royalties.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France applies the Economic Substance Doctrine under general anti-abuse provisions (Article 102 of the French Tax Code, l'abus de droit) and into force through the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD) and the recent DAC6/Ministerial Regulations (loi anti-abus). For the wearable electronics sector, the doctrine requires the French SAS to demonstrate real managerial and operational substance in France: actual hiring of technical and commercial personnel, physical presence of production support and after-sales functions, control over inventory and logistics, commercial decision-making autonomy, and financial substance (bank accounts, treasury management, invoicing and collection). A French SAS that acts as a pure shell or flow-through entity, whose board decisions are effectively made by a foreign parent, and whose assets, functions, and risks are not aligned with reported income, can be disregarded for tax purposes, resulting in reallocation of profits to the non-resident enterprise and full recharacterisation of transactions. The French tax administration also applies the 'substance over form' rule and can invoke the abuse of law procedure (retour à la lettre de la loi) to recharacterise artificial arrangements; mandatory disclosure rules require cross-border arrangements containing hallmarks connected to economic substance to be reported to the French tax authorities. For entities engaging in intercompany distribution of smartwatches, the French administration requires a functional and risk analysis (FAR) demonstrating that the SAS performs the core marketing, warranty, credit risk, and regulatory compliance activities and that it retains a commensurate profit under OECD TP principles.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful filing of false tax returns, fraudulent under-declaration of taxable profits, concealment of substantial turnover from smartwatch sales, or artificial creation of deductible costs via fictitious invoices from related foreign shell suppliers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to EUR 500,000 (up to EUR 2,000,000 in case of aggravated circumstances) and imprisonment up to 5 years; civil penalty under Article 1729 of the CGI equal to 80% of the tax understated where bad faith intent is proven. Automatic publication of administrative sanctions under the 'Name and Shame' scheme, and loss of certain tax advantages and public procurement rights.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing director and de facto directors of the SAS are jointly and severally liable for tax debts if they have participated in the fraud. Under Article L.267 of the Livre des procédures fiscales, a president or general manager who committed fraud or who was grossly negligent in the management of the corporation may be personally liable for all tax penalties and interest. Directors face a travel ban from leaving French territory (interdiction de quitter le territoire) during tax enforcement procedures, an asset freeze order (saisie conservatoire), and criminal imprisonment of up to 5 years for tax fraud. The corporate veil is pierced where the entity is deemed fictitious or the transactions are considered sham; directors lose the limitation liability shield of the SAS.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing the French SAS with no commercial activity, no French management, and no distinct operational substance, using it solely as a conduit to pass intercompany payments (royalties or service fees) out of France to the benefit of the non-resident parent, or to evade permanent establishment and transfer pricing rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The French tax administration may recharacterise the entire structure under Article 1651 of the CGI and the OECD Model Treaty Article on Limitation on Benefits, denying treaty benefits and imposing the 25% withholding on deemed distributions, a 15% withholding on deemed royalties, and reallocating profits to the parent; penalties of 80% for concealed activity and interest at 0.20% per month. Under EU law, the anti-abuse Directive (2016/1164) and OECD BEPS Action 6, the entity may be denied any DTA relief. The corporate entity may also be struck off the French Trade and Companies Register if the French tax authorities or the court determine that the registered head office is fictitious; administrative dissolution of the entity is possible under Article L.235-3 of the Companies Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors knowingly causing the creation of a shell company can face personal obligations for corporate taxes under the judicial liquidation procedure (action en complément de passif) and may be declared personally bankrupt (faillite personnelle) for mixing corporate assets with personal assets, misusing corporate property, or continuing a sham business. The court may order a temporary prohibition on managing any enterprise and a travel ban; the president of the SAS may be regarded as the sole decision-making person and bear full liability for the full amount of unpaid taxes plus damages to creditors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the French manufacturing entity to receive funds of illicit origin from foreign shareholders, conducting high-value smartwatch sales with resilient third-party agents without verifying beneficial owners, or managing the company's cash through opaque intermediaries with no business justification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: France classifies the manufacturing of electronic equipment as part of the non-financial sector subject to AML obligations only if the entity acts as a DNFBP (professionnel de la vente de biens, or auctioneer/casino businesses); however, if the entity is used for laundering the proceeds of tax evasion, the sanction is a criminal fine of up to EUR 750,000 (10% of the laundered principal) and imprisonment up to 10 years under Articles 324-1 to 324-6 of the French Criminal Code. Administrative fines under SARFIG (Service à competence nationale) can reach EUR 5 million or twice the value of the misused assets. French TRACFIN (financial intelligence) will receive reports, and repeat offenders face enhanced penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who participate in laundering or fail to comply with binding AML obligations (KYC, beneficial ownership identification, systematic reporting to TRACFIN for suspicious transactions) are criminally liable; the corporate veil is pierced for wilful blindness. Directors face imprisonment, fines, lifelong prohibition from managing any French company, and freezing of personal assets located in France. With the entry into force of the French Fifth AML Directive transposition (Code monétaire et financier), the inability to prove an honest source of the funds may lead to a presumption of guilt.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure and Related-Party Pricing Adjustment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare or refusing to submit the transfer pricing documentation within 30 days after a formal request by the French tax administration, or entering into intercompany transactions that do not reflect the arm's length principle (e.g., underpricing of contract manufacturing services rendered by the French SAS to the non-resident parent).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty under Article 1735 ter B of the CGI: EUR 15,000 per fiscal year for absence or non-submission of transfer pricing documentation, plus a further EUR 5,000 per undisclosed related enterprise or per incomplete documentation. If documentation is submitted within more than 30 days, the penalty increases to EUR 20,000. If the tax administration adjusts the taxable base, the 40% penalty for lack of good faith applies, and the burden of proof shifts to the taxpayer; the tax adjustment is also subject to interest. For enterprises with revenue above EUR 400 million that fail to file the simplified declaration, the penalty is EUR 150,000 additionally.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The president and other directors of the SAS are personally responsible for ensuring the documentation obligation is fulfilled. If the failure to document is coupled with intentional misrepresentation of intercompany pricing, the directors risk criminal tax fraud charges; the corporate veil can be lifted by a commercial court in the event of gross negligence leading to the company's insolvency (action en responsabilité pour insuffisance d'actif). Where the transfer pricing adjustment results in a criminal conviction, the director may be banned from managing any French company for 5 years and be ordered to restitute the tax savings to the treasury.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Profit Repatriation and Dividend Distribution Without Withholding Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends or deemed dividends to a non-resident shareholder without applying the statutory 25% withholding or without proving treaty entitlement, or discretely channeling profits through excessive management fees or royalties without complying with the withholding obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The French tax administration can reassess the company for the unpaid withholding (retenue à la source), impose a 40% penalty for failure to withhold, plus late interest at 0.20% per month. The company is denied any deduction for the fees or royalties that were deemed concealed distributions. In addition, if the shareholder is a low-tax jurisdiction resident and the anti-abuse rule applies, the withholding rate rises to 75% (Article 119 quater 2 bis) and the recipient is denied all treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approved or executed a distribution without compliance may be jointly liable for the withholding tax debt under the general tax liability provisions and may face the 'responsabilité solidaire' of the tax procedure; if the distribution is legally disguised as a sham, the president and financial director will be personally liable for the entire amount of the unpaid tax and the 40% fraud penalty, and may receive a travel ban under enforcement proceedings.
